caption:
SPF is measured with 2 mg of sunscreen on every square centimetre of skin. Almost nobody applies that much.

When researchers measured what 26 people actually put on their faces, the average was about 1 mg/cm2 - half the test amount. On Danish beaches the number was closer to a quarter: 0.57 mg/cm2, which turned a labelled SPF 20 into an effective SPF of about 2.

The same Danish work tested a simple fix: apply, then apply again. Double application roughly doubled the amount on the skin and cut the area left completely uncovered by more than half.

So before looking for a stronger bottle, it is worth using more of the one you already have.

What this does not mean: these are small studies, one was industry-funded, and effective SPF here is calculated rather than measured on each person. The direction is consistent across all three; the exact numbers will not match everyone.

Le Digabel J et al. Skin Res Technol 2023. doi:10.1111/srt.13320
Heerfordt IM. Dan Med J 2018;65(4):B5476
Wulf HC et al. Photodermatol Photoimmunol Photomed 1997. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0781.1997.tb00215.x
